answer: Most painters don't offer limewash. It is mineral work with its own rules, and Toronto happens to be good territory for it: roughly a third of the housing stock here is pre-1961 brick, which is the surface limewash was made for.
Exterior work on brick generally runs $4 to $8 per square foot in the city. Interior decorative work starts higher. What a real quote costs depends on what shape the wall is in.
If your house sits in a heritage district, read the permit question before you book anything.

verdict.heading: Should you limewash a Toronto house?
paragraphs: The best candidate is unpainted brick, and Toronto has a lot of it. On century brick in Cabbagetown or Harbord Village, limewash is one of the few finishes that actually suits the wall. It breathes with the masonry instead of sealing it, and it can be renewed rather than stripped.

Already painted brick is a different job. Limewash bonds by soaking into porous masonry, and acrylic paint blocks that. What you likely need is a mineral primer system or a german schmear style mortar finish. Anyone quoting you without looking at the substrate first is guessing.

Interior work on drywall or plaster is open to almost any home. A single accent wall is a reasonable weekend if you are handy. A full exterior is not: substrate assessment, weather windows and scaffolding put it firmly in specialist territory.
If you want the look permanently and never want to recoat, price brick staining instead. Just know it is a one way door. Limewash weathers and can be refreshed. Stain is forever.

process.heading: How the work goes
steps: A specialist looks at the wall first: substrate, previous coatings, mortar condition. This is where painted brick and repair problems surface.
A sample panel goes up on your actual wall. Limewash reads differently on every brick, and nobody serious skips this step.
You get a firm quote by surface area and condition. The ranges on this page are a sanity check, not the quote.
Exterior work gets booked into a weather window, which means scheduling ahead of the season rather than during it.
Application is usually two coats with cure time between. Expect days, not hours, and expect the finish to settle into a patina. That is the material working as designed.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to limewash a house in Toronto?
faqs.a: Outside a heritage district, no. Limewash is finish work, not construction. But Toronto has 27 Heritage Conservation Districts, including Cabbagetown, Wychwood Park, Harbord Village, South Rosedale and Kensington Market. Inside one, changing an exterior finish can require a heritage permit. Check your address against the city's heritage map before you book exterior work.

faqs.q: What does limewash cost in Toronto?
faqs.a: Exterior limewash on brick generally lands between $4 and $8 per square foot, with broader exterior work quoted up to about $12. Decorative interior application starts around $12. Add HST. The spread comes down to surface condition, access and how much prep the wall needs, which is why the sample panel and site visit matter before anyone commits to a number.

faqs.q: Can you limewash brick that has already been painted?
faqs.a: Not directly. Limewash works by soaking into porous masonry, and a coat of acrylic paint stops it from getting in. Painted brick usually means a mineral primer system or a german schmear style finish instead. This is the single most common reason a limewash quote changes after the site visit.

faqs.q: Why limewash instead of masonry paint?
faqs.a: Limewash is breathable. Moisture in an old solid masonry wall escapes through it instead of blistering underneath a sealed film, which is exactly what those walls need. It also ages by softening rather than peeling. The trade off is a finish that weathers and wants renewal every several years. If you want a static, uniform film and are fine repainting on a cycle, masonry paint is the honest choice.

faqs.q: When should exterior limewash happen in Toronto?
faqs.a: May through September is the dependable stretch. April can work late in the month once frost risk fades, and October only early, before the first frost comes back around the start of November. Rain falls on about a quarter of days through the season, so the actual cure window is always a forecast call. Late summer gives the best odds of a dry run. Book in spring for the season rather than trying to squeeze in during it.
